assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new topological classification of insulating states, with the quantum spin Hall effect predicted from clean symmetry arguments and then seen in transport. It is an unusually complete theory-to-experiment chain, and it shaped a large part of modern condensed matter physics. The discovery is clear and conceptually original.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction and the Z2 classification. Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. That proposal is not among the credited names, which leaves a real credit question, but the three listed names still make a coherent prize.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations exist across several material platforms, and the interpretation has been stable for over fifteen years. Recognition is timely. The 2016 prize on topological phases covered a neighbouring but distinct body of work.
uncertainties: Whether the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (not in the credited names) is acceptable.
Overlap with the topological-phase prize of 2016 may be read as redundant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum mechanics into a practical protocol whose security rests on physical law. The idea is original and clear, and it has had lasting impact on quantum communication. It follows naturally from the entanglement experiments recognised in 2022.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84, and Ekert introduced the entanglement-based protocol, so all three made decisive and distinct contributions. A three-way prize is feasible. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a possible complication that is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fiber and satellite demonstrations have confirmed the protocols in practice. The principle is well established. Recognition is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether this is physics enough or information science, and whether the committee wants to follow 2022 this soon.
Wiesner's precedence and the practical security of real implementations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy. This is a genuine discovery of a new messenger and sits at the centre of what the Prize rewards.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual leader of the IceCube concept. Karle and Spiering made key contributions to the detector and the analysis. A large collaboration complicates attribution, and the proposed three are defensible rather than uniquely correct.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established. Source identification is still partial, and the interpretation of the individual sources is still developing. The discovery is mature but its astrophysical payoff is not yet complete.
uncertainties: The choice of laureates among a very large collaboration is contested.
Source associations other than the first blazar are still incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level. They make a new standard of time and open tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The invention is original and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the magic-wavelength lattice. Ye brought it to record precision and set the benchmark for the field. Two laureates give a clean configuration. Overlap with the frequency-comb prize of 2005 is the main allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: The clocks have been independently reproduced in several laboratories and a redefinition of the second is under discussion. The work is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether others, such as Lemonde or Ludlow, deserve recognition, and the extent to which this builds on the 2005 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene gave a tunable platform for correlated insulators, superconductivity and topological states, with a theoretical prediction that was verified. The prediction-then-discovery sequence is striking and the field is very active.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of the flat bands. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery in 2018. The credit is clean for these three, while Cao and the other co-authors are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation by many independent groups is strong. The nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet settled. Recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity is not yet resolved.
The prize could be seen as early for a young field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fast radio bursts are a new class of millisecond extragalactic radio transients that probe the intergalactic medium. The discovery of the Lorimer burst was unexpected and is cleanly stated. The impact is considerable because of the cosmological uses.
assessment.attribution: Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes were the core of the 2007 discovery. Confirmation by Thornton and colleagues, and later work on repeating and localized bursts, was also decisive, and the credit around the discovery is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Hundreds to thousands of bursts are catalogued and hosts have been localized, including the Galactic SGR 1935+2154 burst. The physical origin of the population is still unsettled. The phenomenon is established, but the interpretation is not yet stable.
uncertainties: The progenitor mechanism is still unknown.
Credit between the original discovery, the confirmation and the localization work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory gave exact results for two-dimensional critical phenomena and underlies string worldsheet theory. It is a deep and original framework with a lasting impact on statistical physics and high-energy theory. As a theorist I admire it, but the Prize emphasizes discoveries confirmed in nature.
assessment.attribution: Polyakov and Zamolodchikov, together with Belavin, produced the central BPZ construction, and Cardy connected it to critical phenomena and finite-size scaling. Belavin is missing from the credited names, which makes the attribution awkward.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and thoroughly validated in statistical models. Its experimental confirmation is indirect and spread over many systems. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Belavin's role is not represented among the credited names.
Whether this is a discovery about nature or a mathematical framework, and its relation to the committee's emphasis on experimental confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong coupling between a superconducting qubit and a microwave resonator, giving a scalable architecture for quantum computing and readout. The concept is clear and its impact on quantum technology is large.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues supplied the theoretical proposal, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf delivered the first experimental realization. The trio is natural. The earlier work on superconducting circuits is already recognised.
assessment.maturity: The architecture has been adopted widely and confirmed independently. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits recently rewarded a neighbouring field, which may reduce the urgency here.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
Whether the technological impact rather than a new discovery of nature fits the Prize.
